A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoVoMix2 work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The new Appendix C and the relocated older appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original dialogue and monologue evaluations, a listener study, speaker-consistency analyses, and training ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on prompt length, generated dialogue length, and real-world conversational prompts.

M1.justification: The architecture, speaker streams, alignment, masking, flow-matching objective, training strategy, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that the existing speaker markers act as indicators replacing prompt transcriptions; it does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds NCSSD-CEN conversational prompts with natural prosody and background noise, extending evaluation beyond clean LibriSpeech prompts. Short-prompt conditions are also explicitly tested, while the training corpora and underlying English dialogue and monologue tasks remain.

E2.justification: MoonCast and Sesame remain the numerical baselines, including in the new experiments. Figure 5 retains the qualitative comparisons with NotebookLM and CoVoMix; newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C substantially expands the evaluation design: prompt trimming uses 20 speakers and 100 DailyDialog dialogues, duration testing uses four authored dialogues at 30–120 seconds, and conversational prompts come from 10 dialogues. Section 5.2 changes its reported sample from one to three 12-turn dialogues. The prompt range is described as 3–18 seconds, although Figure 6 also plots 20 seconds. Original training settings and headline evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests sensitivity to prompt duration, extrapolation to longer generated conversations, and robustness to conversational prompts containing noise. These materially expand robustness and failure-condition analysis. The earlier data-mixing, training-stage, and silence-token ablations are retained in Appendix D.

E5.justification: The standard-deviation reporting in Tables 1 and 3 is unchanged. No new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced. The increase to three dialogues is an evaluation sample-size change.

E6.justification: Figure 6 and Tables 4–5 add substantial robustness results. On conversational prompts, CoVoMix2 reports SA-WER 9.32 versus 26.26 for MoonCast and 25.19 for Sesame; Table 4 records Sesame failing at 120 seconds. Figure 4(a) replaces the plotted curves and now ranks CoVoMix2 highest throughout, alongside the changed dialogue sample. Existing headline, monologue, and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, flow-matching loss, and classifier-free guidance equations are unchanged. Neither version adds formal results or proofs beyond the retained formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about fully non-autoregressive generation, transcription-free speaker prompts, controllable overlap, quality, speaker consistency, and efficiency. The new experiments support existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C add interpretations about robustness to prompt length and generation beyond training durations, together with discussion of degradation in longer conversations. Section 6 describes stability to approximately 90 seconds more strongly than Table 4 supports. The existing limitations concerning transcription noise and simulated overlap remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 identifies previously unnamed services as Microsoft speech enhancement and Microsoft Fast Transcription, labels the podcast corpus as internal, and adds a link to an open-source data-preparation pipeline. These improve documented provenance and reproducibility without establishing changes to the underlying processing tools.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to VoiceLDM, DiTTo-TTS, DailyTalk, and Moshi. The broader positioning relative to autoregressive, hybrid, and conversational speech-synthesis approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized clarifications, an expanded Section 6, and a new Appendix C, with older appendices relettered. The publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel Figure 6 and two result tables, and revises Figure 4's legend and axis presentation. Existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered, with modest page reflow; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through targeted robustness tests and improves reproducibility by identifying processing services and linking data-preparation code. These gains are limited by the small duration study and overstated interpretation: Section 6 claims stability to about 90 seconds, while Table 4 reports SA-WER rising from 5.88 at 60 seconds to 14.74 at 90 seconds. The additions nevertheless provide useful evidence about applicability and failure conditions.
